topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture series, outlines the speaker's background, and introduces the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: The Biological and Evolutionary Nature of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a clonal, evolutionary disease driven by genetic mutations, microenvironmental factors, and intrinsic cellular processes.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate external cancer risk factors, the debate surrounding intrinsic chance versus external causation, and global epidemiological patterns of cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the role of viral, bacterial, and parasitic infections in driving cancer, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mechanisms of DNA Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce DNA adducts and mutations directly or through metabolic activation.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation versus Promotion in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate between mutational initiators and non-mutagenic promoters that drive tumorigenesis through inflammation and sustained cell proliferation.

topics.label: Host Cell Susceptibility and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how target tissue states and developmental windows modulate cancer susceptibility, concluding with a synthesis of carcinogenic mechanisms.

topics.label: Methods for Identifying Carcinogens and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, experimental, and risk-assessment methodologies used to identify carcinogens and evaluate cancer etiology.
